newsitem.title: UK: Britain to give passports to Hong Kong minorities.
newsitem.headline: Britain to give passports to Hong Kong minorities.

text.p: The British government on Tuesday bowed to pressure from members of parliament and from Hong Kong and said it would give passports to as many as 8,000 mainly Indian and Pakistani residents of the colony.

Home Secretary Michael Howard said he had carefully reviewed the position of Hong Kong's ethnic minorities in light of concern that their nationality would be uncertain after the British colony reverts to China at midnight on June 30.
"It is clear that the assurances which they have been given over a number of years have not allayed this concern," Howard, the interior minister, told parliament.

"I therefore intend to make provision enabling them to apply for registration as British citizens, giving them the right of abode in the United Kingdom after 30 June 1997," he said in a written answer.
Howard said he expected the great majority of those concerned to continue to live in Hong Kong.
The prospect of British citizenship, leaked in Tuesday's British press, was earlier welcomed by representatives of Hong Kong's non-Chinese residents, who faced possible statelessness.
